anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch) the USB-C VBUS pin J14.A4 is wired to a net that carries BOTH the +5V power port and a global 'VBUS' label. On the Power sheet (power.kicad_sch) the TPS2121RUXR (U10) IN2 (pin 2) is on +5V and OUT (pin 1) is on VBUS. Because J14.A4 joins the two names, the +5V rail and the internal VBUS rail are shorted together, tying the mux output directly to its IN2 and to the USB VBUS pin.
anomalies.expected: The two rails must be separate: the USB VBUS pin feeds only +5V (mux IN2), and the mux OUT feeds only the internal pre-buck VBUS rail. The spec states 'J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2)' and 'note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.'

evidence.quote: J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2).
outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail - note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux).

mcu.kicad_sch, sheet /Microcontroller/, page 1: J14 USB_C_Receptacle pin A4 wire carries '+5V' power port and 'VBUS' global label; power.kicad_sch, sheet /Power/, page 1: U10 pin 2 IN2 = '+5V', pin 1 OUT = 'VBUS'.

anomalies.impact: The power mux arbitration is defeated: USB VBUS is hard-wired to the pre-buck rail and to the mux output. With the barrel jack connected, the mux OUT (12 V) back-feeds into the +5V net and out through the USB-C VBUS pin, over-volting the USB port / host and bypassing the seamless-switchover the design relies on; with USB only, the mux does nothing. The headline 'power mux arbitrates the two supplies' protection is lost.
